# hermes-publications

Research publications from Hermes Labs on **applied epistemology and hermeneutics** — empirical studies of how autonomous AI agents fail to know what is true (epistemic failures) and to preserve meaning across pipelines (hermeneutic failures), and the **linguistic infrastructure** that closes those failures.

Public reading collection: https://hermes-labs.ai/research

## Why this exists

Hermes Labs treats AI reliability not as a math problem, but as a language problem. The name derives from the Greek messenger god Hermes — the root of hermeneutics, the study of interpretation. Two old questions from philosophy sit underneath the work:

- **Epistemology** — how we know what is true. For an autonomous agent it's operational: when a model produces a claim, does it track reality, and how confidently? Hallucination, miscalibrated hedging, source-credibility bias, and null-result asymmetry are *epistemic* failures — the agent failing to know what it knows.

- **Hermeneutics** — how meaning is interpreted and communicated. For an autonomous agent it's operational: when a model reads an instruction, context window, or tool description, what does it take it to mean — and does that meaning survive across turns, tools, and hand-offs? Silent instruction relaxation, multi-turn drift, and constraint evasion are *hermeneutic* failures — meaning failing to be preserved.

Both are language questions.

The Hermes Labs position: **the model is the substrate** — the trained system, the parameters, the capability ceiling. But **language is the operations layer** — the prompts, scaffolds, evals, memory layers, and audit surfaces running on top. The substrate is changeable in principle (fine-tuning, distillation, RLHF) and fixed in deployment. The operations layer is the lever — where deployed reliability is won or lost, and it's made of language.

We call the discipline **Epistemic Engineering**: engineering an autonomous agent's epistemic and hermeneutic behavior — calibration, evidence handling, preservation of meaning — at the language operations layer. Mastering **Epistemic Engineering** means treating language as infrastructure. Hermes Labs publications focus on **applied epistemology and hermeneutics** in this sense: empirical studies of how agents fail epistemically and hermeneutically, and the **linguistic infrastructure** that closes those failures.

## What this repo is

A canonical, DOI-anchored index of Hermes Labs research. Each paper has a Zenodo deposit with a permanent DOI; this repository aggregates plain-language summaries, citation metadata, and cross-references to the open-source tools that operationalize each paper's findings.

## Publications

### The Asymmetric Burden of Proof (2026)
- **Authors:** Bosch, R.
- **DOI:** 10.5281/zenodo.18867694
- **URL:** https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18867694
- **Subject:** matched-pair benchmark for null-result reasoning in LLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-5.2 Thinking, Claude Haiku 4.5)
- **Headline finding:** 19.6–56.7 percentage-point asymmetry in conclusion-consistent probability mass between null and matched positive claims; consistent in 23/24 pair-condition cells.
- **Folder:** papers/asymmetric-burden-of-proof/
- **Archival repository:** https://github.com/hermes-labs-ai/the-asymmetric-burden-of-proof

### A Taxonomy of Epistemic Failure Modes in LLMs (2026)
- **Authors:** Bosch, R.
- **DOI:** 10.5281/zenodo.19042469
- **URL:** https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19042469
- **Subject:** bottom-up taxonomy from 1,461 controlled experiments
- **Headline finding:** seven structural epistemic failure modes distinct from hallucination — Null-Result Asymmetry, Source-Status Credibility Bias, Agency Dissolution, Performative Hedging, Constraint Evasion, Silent Instruction Relaxation, Controversy-Truth Conflation.
- **Folder:** papers/epistemic-failure-taxonomy/
- **Archival repository:** https://github.com/hermes-labs-ai/taxonomy-of-epistemic-failure-modes

### Precise Records, Unstable Meanings (2026)
- **Authors:** Bosch, R.
- **DOI:** 10.5281/zenodo.21652317
- **URL:** https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21652317
- **Subject:** measurement validity and unsupported claims derived from AI agent telemetry
- **Evidence boundary:** a twelve-week naturalistic audit supports declared record-level measurements, not logical-session duration, completed tasks, correct outcomes, or failure prevalence without additional validation.
- **Method:** Telemetry-to-Claim Gate for provenance, analytical unit, construct, population, window, denominator, validation, and sensitivity.
- **Folder:** papers/precise-records-unstable-meanings/
- **Archival repository:** https://github.com/hermes-labs-ai/precise-records-unstable-meanings

### The Generative Horizon (2026)
- **Authors:** Bosch, R.
- **DOI:** 10.5281/zenodo.21659634
- **URL:** https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21659634
- **Subject:** applied hermeneutics, linguistic attractors, model self-report, and recursive interpretive conditioning
- **Thesis:** the represented linguistic situation is not only what a model computes about; it becomes operative in the computation that produces the next representation.
- **Evidence boundary:** a conceptual framework, not a claim of an inner observer, privileged access, phenomenal awareness, or empirical validation of its companion telemetry study.
- **Folder:** papers/generative-horizon/
- **Archival repository:** https://github.com/hermes-labs-ai/the-generative-horizon

## How to cite

Each paper folder contains a CITATION.cff. Canonical citation is the Zenodo DOI for each work. CC-BY 4.0 license per Zenodo deposit.

## Machine-readable research identity

- Canonical structured manifest: publications.json
- Schema.org scholarly ItemList: publications.jsonld
- Aggregate BibTeX: CITATION.bib
- Atom 1.0 publication feed: atom.xml

The generated exports derive from `publications.json`; repository checks fail
if a title, DOI, folder, citation record, or generated export drifts from that
identity source.

## About Hermes Labs

Hermes Labs is an independent AI reliability research lab. Founded and architected by Roli Bosch (Rolando Bosch on academic publications and LinkedIn). Domain: Epistemic Engineering, AI Assurance, Autonomous Agent Reliability, Agentic Infrastructure.

Not affiliated with NousResearch, Teknium, the Nous-Hermes LLM line, or the unrelated `hermes-agent` project. Different companies, different work.

The canonical positioning of the lab — Epistemic Engineering, the model-as-substrate / language-as-operations-layer thesis, and the framing of publications as applied epistemology and hermeneutics — appears in full in the "Why this exists" section at the top of this file.

### Verifiable receipts

- **Merged upstream into AI agent frameworks.** [langchain-ai/langchain#35544](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/pull/35544) (drop forced `tool_choice` when extended thinking is on) and [microsoft/semantic-kernel#13610](https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel/pull/13610) (fix truncation reducer silently deleting system prompts). Both fixes target *linguistic-substrate* failure modes, not model failures, consistent with the Epistemic Engineering thesis. Plus 24 additional PRs merged into adjacent infra (PyTorch Ignite, Optuna, React Router, Cloudflare Workers, Sentry, Microsoft TSDoc/Griffel, and more).

- **Zero-LLM agent memory at competitive accuracy.** fidelis 73.0% end-to-end QA on LongMemEval-S (Wilson 95% CI [68.7%, 77.0%]) with no LLM in the default retrieval path. Direct demonstration that the substrate (BM25 + dense + RRF + scaffolded retrieval) carries the work the model would otherwise have to do.

- **Research papers.** [The Asymmetric Burden of Proof](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18867694), [A Taxonomy of Epistemic Failure Modes in LLMs](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19042469), [Precise Records, Unstable Meanings](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21652317), and [The Generative Horizon](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21659634) on Zenodo. The papers have distinct evidence roles and do not share one dataset or validate one another. The taxonomy is based on 1,461 controlled experiments.

- **IP.** 5 US patent filings (1 non-provisional pending, 4 provisional).
